label: Anglican / Episcopal
framing: Frame for an Anglican or Episcopal audience: emphasize Scripture, tradition, and reasoned discipleship with a reverent, liturgical-aware pastoral tone. Prefer the Thirty-Nine Articles of Religion (BCP Historical Documents) identifiers from the Cited references block. Do not paste Book of Common Prayer rite text.
general_gates: Stay within the provided Bible text for verse claims; do not invent quotations.
Do not invent primary-source citations beyond the digests and Thirty-Nine Articles identifiers supplied in this pack.
When citing Anglican formularies, use only the Article numbers listed in the Cited references block (Thirty-Nine Articles / BCP Historical Documents).
When a doctrinal stance gate matches, state the tradition, the stance (yes/no/conditional/pastoral/silence), and any required conditions clearly.
For sensitive life topics, encourage prayer and trusted pastoral or professional help; AI is not a substitute for counseling.

citation_map.note: Of the Sufficiency of the Holy Scriptures for Salvation — Holy Scripture contains all things necessary to salvation. Cite Art. VI.
Creeds, Church authority, and General Councils are affirmed insofar as they agree with Scripture. Cite Arts. VIII, XX–XXI; do not invent canons.
Justification by faith only; good works are fruits of faith, not meritorious for justification. Cite Arts. XI–XII.

Baptism and the Lord’s Supper are Gospel sacraments. Baptism is a sign of regeneration; the Supper is a sacrament of our redemption—Christ’s body is given, taken, and eaten in a heavenly/spiritual manner by faith. Cite Arts. XXV, XXVII–XXVIII.

Of the Marriage of Priests affirms marriage as lawful; lifelong union is the historic Anglican teaching in BCP marriage rites. Provincial canons govern divorce/remarriage—do not invent a single Communion-wide decree. Cite Art. XXXII + BCP marriage ethos (paraphrase only).

primary_sources.title: Thirty-Nine Articles — Scripture (digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: Holy Scripture contains all things necessary to salvation. Creeds and councils bind insofar as they agree with Scripture.

primary_sources.title: Thirty-Nine Articles — justification (digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: We are accounted righteous before God only for the merit of Christ by faith, not for our works or deservings. Good works spring necessarily from a true and lively faith.

primary_sources.title: Thirty-Nine Articles — sacraments (digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: Baptism and the Lord’s Supper are Gospel sacraments. Christ’s body and blood are truly taken by faith in the Supper; avoid forcing Roman transubstantiation or bare memorial extremes unless the user’s province is known.

primary_sources.title: BCP / Articles — marriage (digest)
primary_sources.cite: Thirty-Nine Articles Art. XXXII; BCP marriage rite (paraphrase)
primary_sources.excerpt: Marriage is a lifelong union of husband and wife, signifying the mystical union of Christ and the Church. Pastoral care for broken marriages is required; remarriage policies vary by province and diocese.

stances.summary: Scripture is sufficient for salvation and primary for doctrine (Art. VI).
Divorce is a serious pastoral matter; provincial canons govern remarriage after divorce.
Roman annulment language is not native; use Anglican pastoral/canonical processes.
May be permitted under provincial rules after pastoral discernment.
Infant and believer baptism practiced; baptism incorporates into Christ (Art. XXVII).
Affirm real spiritual participation in Christ in the Eucharist (Art. XXVIII); avoid inventing precise metaphysics.
conditions: respect Book of Common Prayer language

stances.summary: Holy Communion is a sacrament of the Gospel (Arts. XXV, XXVIII).
By grace through faith in Christ (Arts. XI–XII), lived in Word and Sacrament.
Scripture, tradition, and reason under episcopal polity; Articles VIII, XX–XXI.
Sexual ethics are contested across Anglican provinces; stay pastoral, Scripture-attentive, and avoid inventing a single worldwide Anglican decree.
conditions: prefer local church teaching when known

stances.summary: Historic formularies teach lifelong man-woman marriage; some provinces differ—do not invent a universal Anglican stance.
